name: Reliable outbound — PH + HN + G2(Apify) → LinkFinder → Instantly

nodes.name: Every hour
nodes.notes: Hourly, not daily. The whole reliability model is repetition: a provider that answers half the time covers ~97% of a queue after five attempts. Daily would take five days to do what this does in five hours.

nodes.name: Hacker News: Show HN
nodes.notes: No credential at all. The one source here that cannot fail on auth, which is exactly why it is worth keeping even at low yield.

nodes.name: LinkFinder: decision maker
nodes.notes: Three in-request retries handle a momentary flake. Anything still unresolved goes back on the queue. If a company simply has no findable decision maker, that is a normal outcome, not an error — it is marked done and the run continues.

nodes.name: Usable, retry, or done with it

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ campaign: $json.campaignId, email: $json.email, first_name: $json.firstName, last_name: $json.lastName, company_name: $json.company, website: $json.domain, skip_if_in_workspace: true, custom_variables: { observation: $json.observation, category: $json.category, source: $json.source, title: $json.title } }) }}

nodes.name: Instantly: add lead
nodes.notes: observation is the merge field the opener renders. It is composed at source time so the sentence is true of wherever the lead actually came from — never a hard-coded 'on G2'.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ query: 'query { posts(order: NEWEST, first: 50) { edges { node { id name tagline website votesCount createdAt topics(first: 2) { edges { node { name } } } } } } }' }) }}

nodes.name: Product Hunt: recent launches
nodes.notes: v2 GraphQL — v1 was deprecated in 2023. Free developer token from your app's page on api.producthunt.com. Complexity limit is 1000, which is why topics is capped at 2 and makers/comments are not requested.

nodes.name: Apify: G2 products
nodes.notes: run-sync-get-dataset-items returns the actor's dataset directly, so there is no run to poll. The token goes in the query string because that is what this endpoint accepts. Actors differ in what they call their fields — the normaliser accepts several spellings rather than assuming one. Verify the input shape against your chosen actor before trusting a scheduled run.
